analysis:
The only changed region in SSDPrefixCache.swift is evictOldestEntry (base 1773-1787, head 1773-1778). The inline victim loop is replaced by a call to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:) with a closure that builds the block URL from the HMAC tag and calls retireIndexedEntries([url]). Deletion still goes through retireIndexedEntries, which takes removalLock and checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot. It also uses SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove with the root, index and epochStore, and reconcileExternalRemovals runs on external change. The hasSafeRoot guard at line 1772 is unchanged. The stats update is preserved: evictions is incremented when freed > 0.

The new evictOldest helper is not in the supplied evidence, so these points are unverified:
- Whether it preserves the old semantics of dropping invalid or missing entries.
- Whether it skips a valid but undeletable victim and tries the next one.
- Whether it stops on externalChange (the old code returned 0).
- Whether its victim iteration is bounded.

If the helper regresses, the likely impact is that box-wide disk-budget enforcement stalls (availability and at-rest retention, T-041 mitigation (b), SEC-035 scope). That would be an unverified contract, not an observed regression, so I raise no finding. The unchanged donate and stage paths (the 30-minute TTL, HMAC tags, cacheSalt folding, reservation release) were read and show no change in at-rest exposure. No ciphertext, key or tag handling changed. Integration should check SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest in the file that defines it.
